title: NY State Assembly · District 74
area: Manhattan's East Side, including Stuyvesant Town, Peter Cooper Village, Murray Hill, Kips Bay and Gramercy.

context.text: The seat became vacant when Harvey Epstein (D) resigned after winning election to the New York City Council. Keith Powers (D), the term-limited outgoing City Council Majority Leader for the adjoining district, won a February 3, 2026 special election for the seat, defeating Joseph Foley (R, C) 82.5% to 16.5%. Powers is now the Democratic nominee for a full term; Veronica Gonzalez (R, C) is his general-election opponent, having advanced unopposed through the canceled Republican and Conservative Party primaries.

candidates.name: Keith Powers
candidates.currentRole: Former New York City Council Member (2018-2025)

summary.text: Keith Powers is the Democratic nominee for a full term representing NY State Assembly District 74. A lifelong Manhattan resident and former government-relations executive, he served on the New York City Council for the 4th District from 2018 to 2025, including as Majority Leader, before winning the February 2026 special election to succeed Harvey Epstein. His official biography highlights housing and tenant issues.

background.text: Born November 16, 1983, in New York City, according to Wikipedia; his official biography says he is a lifelong Manhattan resident, born and raised in Stuyvesant Town and Peter Cooper Village, where he lives today, and a third-generation resident of the complex.
Earned a B.A. in political science from the University of Dayton and an M.A. in political science from the CUNY Graduate Center; his official biography says he attended both institutions.
From 2006 to 2011 was chief of staff to then-Assemblyman Jonathan Bing, and was campaign manager for state Sen. Liz Krueger's 2006 campaign.

From January 2011 until his 2017 council campaign was vice president of the government-relations consulting firm Constantinople & Vallone Consulting; he also chaired the Community Board 6 Business Affairs and Street Life Committee and was a district leader for the Eleanor Roosevelt Democratic Club.

Served on the New York City Council representing the 4th District on the East Side of Manhattan from 2018 until being term-limited out of office in 2025; Wikipedia lists him as Council Majority Leader from 2022 to 2024.

His official biography cites his work on office-to-housing conversions and a Midtown South rezoning, a 2019 rent reduction negotiated with senior residents of Waterside Plaza, and a tenant lawsuit over rent stabilization at Stuyvesant Town and Peter Cooper Village.
Won the Manhattan Democratic county committee's nomination in December 2025 to succeed Harvey Epstein, who had moved to the City Council.
Won the February 3, 2026 special election for Assembly District 74 with 82.5% of the vote, defeating Republican/Conservative candidate Joseph Foley, and assumed office February 4, 2026.
Assembly committee assignments are Cities, Correction, People with Disabilities, Racing and Wagering, and Tourism, Parks, Arts and Sports Development.

priorities.text: Converting office space to housing, including new rezoning to allow conversions in Midtown South.
Preventing housing discrimination and protecting tenants from rent overcharges.
Defending rent stabilization for tenants against attempts to weaken it.

positions.summary: As a City Council member, passed legislation to prevent housing discrimination and protect renters from overcharges, negotiated a rent reduction for Waterside Plaza senior tenants, and joined Stuyvesant Town/Peter Cooper Village tenants in a successful lawsuit to preserve their buildings' rent stabilization.
Has led efforts to convert underused office buildings to housing, including a rezoning enabling conversions in Midtown South.
positions.quote: He has been leading the charge on office conversions to housing, including a new rezoning in Midtown South.

record.text: Won the February 3, 2026 special general election for Assembly District 74 with 82.5% of the vote against Joseph Foley (R, C).
As a City Council member, helped negotiate a rent reduction for senior tenants at Waterside Plaza in 2019.
As a City Council member, joined Stuyvesant Town and Peter Cooper Village tenants in a successful lawsuit to maintain rent stabilization for the complex's residents.
As a City Council member, passed legislation preventing housing discrimination and protecting renters from rent overcharges.

candidates.researchNotes: Powers has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and only assumed this Assembly seat in February 2026, so his legislative record here consists mainly of two recent floor votes; most documented record and positions come from his prior eight years on the New York City Council, which are on his official Assembly biography page.

candidates.name: Veronica Gonzalez

summary.text: Veronica Gonzalez is the Republican and Conservative Party nominee challenging incumbent Keith Powers for NY State Assembly District 74. She is a Lower East Side-raised community advocate, small-business owner and Republican district leader who has not previously held elected office.

background.text: Born and raised on the Lower East Side of Manhattan.
Describes herself as a community advocate, Republican district leader, small business owner and author.
Says she has spent decades doing nonprofit-partnership and community-outreach work, including donating backpacks and school supplies and helping secure direct assistance for NYC families.
Says she has assisted NYCHA tenants with apartment-repair backlog issues and received the President's Volunteer Service Award and a Presidential Lifetime Achievement Award.

priorities.text: Restoring public safety and reversing bail-reform policies she says have made communities less safe.
priorities.quote: Restoring public safety, bail reform, and ending policies that make communities less safe

priorities.text: Supporting small businesses she says are burdened by excessive regulation and taxes.
Repealing congestion pricing and related tolls.
Passing e-bike safety regulations, which she calls "Priscilla's Law."
Reforming state guardianship laws and homeless-services/NGO oversight.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for repealing congestion pricing and the tolls that come with it.
Campaign platform calls for restoring public safety and rolling back bail-reform policies she says have made communities less safe.
positions.quote: Restoring public safety, bail reform, and ending policies that make communities less safe

positions.summary: Campaign platform frames small businesses as burdened by excessive regulation and taxes, and criticizes what she calls "failed socialist policies" as harmful to New York.
positions.quote: Fighting back against socialism and failed socialist policies that wreck New York

candidates.researchNotes: Gonzalez has not held elected office and has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; her background and positions above are drawn entirely from her own campaign website, which does not list formal educational credentials or specific dates for her community work.
